prompt.brief: Design a ride ETA and location-sharing service that combines route/traffic data with live driver positions, serves smooth updates to riders, and handles GPS noise, reconnects, and trip privacy.
successSignals: Define trip ownership, route/version, GPS sample quality, map matching, traffic snapshot, ETA confidence, location cadence, and visibility TTL.
Partition by trip/region, smooth noisy or delayed positions, throttle fan-out, and keep driver/rider reads consistent enough without blocking movement.
Separate location ingestion from ETA computation, routing-provider calls, rider WebSocket fan-out, history, and analytics.
Explain reconnect replay, provider outage, trip cancellation, privacy, spoofing, observability, and cached/coarse ETA fallback.

functional: Create trips, accept authenticated driver positions, map-match them, calculate ETA from route/traffic, and share authorized live location.
Support rider/driver reconnects, trip states, route changes, pickup/dropoff, location freshness, notifications, and trip history.
Handle duplicate/out-of-order GPS samples, provider retries, trip deletion/retention, privacy controls, and region failover.
nonFunctional: Deliver fresh location updates every few seconds and serve ETA reads with p95 under 300ms when route providers are healthy.
Scale to 5M active trips and reconnect bursts without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 5M active trips, 1M position updates per second, and 10M concurrent subscribers
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Ride ETA commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Ride ETA writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Ride ETA version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Ride ETA by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Ride ETA work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Ride ETA projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Ride ETA projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Ride ETA records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Ride ETA latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
